:::{#thm-best-predictor}
#### Conditional mean minimizes squared-error risk

Let $\Predvar$ and $\Outvar$ be [jointly distributed](random-variables.qmd#def-jointly-distributed) random variables with $\E{\Outvar^2} < \infty$.
Let $\truemeanf{\Predvar} \eqdef \E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}$ be the [conditional expectation function](#def-cond-expectation-function) of $\Outvar$ given $\Predvar$.
Write $\bestpredfn \eqdef \truemean$ for the prediction function that uses it.
Then for any [prediction function](#def-prediction) $\predfnf{\Predvar}$ with $\E{\predfnf{\Predvar}^2} < \infty$:

$$\popriskf{\predfn} \ge \popriskf{\bestpredfn}$$

with equality if and only if $\P(\predfnf{\Predvar} = \bestpredfnf{\Predvar}) = 1$.
That is, $\bestpredfn$ minimizes the [squared-error risk](#def-squared-error-risk) among all prediction functions of $\Predvar$.

:::

::: proof

By @thm-risk-decomposition:

$$
\ba
\popriskf{\predfn} - \popriskf{\bestpredfn}
&= \E{\sqf{\predfnf{\Predvar} - \bestpredfnf{\Predvar}}}
&& \text{(squared-error risk decomposition)} \\
&\ge 0
&& \text{(the expectation of a non-negative variable)}
\ea
$$

The expectation of the non-negative variable $\sqf{\predfnf{\Predvar} - \bestpredfnf{\Predvar}}$ is zero
if and only if the variable is $0$ with probability $1$,
meaning $\P(\predfnf{\Predvar} = \bestpredfnf{\Predvar}) = 1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-best-predictor}
#### The best predictor in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor,
consider the constant [prediction](#def-prediction) $\predfn_1\paren{\Predvar} = 3$.
Its [squared-error risk](#def-squared-error-risk) is $\popriskf{\predfn_1} = 5$.
The risk of the conditional mean is $\popriskf{\bestpredfn} = 1$.
So $\predfn_1$ has the larger risk.
The inequality is strict because $\predfn_1\paren{\Predvar} \ne \bestpredfnf{\Predvar}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-irreducible-risk}
#### Residual risk (irreducible risk)

The **residual risk** (also called the **irreducible risk**)
is the [squared-error risk](#def-squared-error-risk) of the [conditional expectation function](#def-cond-expectation-function) $\truemean$ of @thm-risk-decomposition:

$$\popriskf{\truemean} = \E{\sqf{\prederrf{\truemean}}}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#thm-irreducible-risk-cond-variance}
#### The residual risk is the expected conditional variance

Let $\Predvar$ and $\Outvar$ be as in @thm-best-predictor.
Then the [residual risk](#def-irreducible-risk) is the [expectation](#def-expectation) of the [conditional variance](#def-cond-variance) of $\Outvar$ given $\Predvar$:

$$
\popriskf{\truemean} = \E{\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}}.
$$ {#eq-irreducible-risk-cond-variance}

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\popriskf{\truemean}
&= \E{\sqf{\prederrf{\truemean}}}
&& \text{(definition of the residual risk)} \\
&= \E{\sqf{\truemeanf{\Predvar} - \Outvar}}
&& \text{(definition of the prediction error)} \\
&= \E{\sqf{\Outvar - \truemeanf{\Predvar}}}
&& \text{(a square is unchanged by negation)} \\
&= \E{\sqf{\Outvar - \E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}}}
&& \text{(definition of } \truemean \text{)} \\
&= \E{\condE{\sqf{\Outvar - \E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}}}{\Predvar}}
&& \text{(law of total expectation)} \\
&= \E{\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}}
&& \text{(definition of conditional variance)}
\ea
$$

:::

::: {#rem-irreducible-risk}
#### The residual risk does not depend on the prediction function

The residual risk depends only on the [joint distribution](random-variables.qmd#def-joint-distribution) of $(\Predvar, \Outvar)$
and not on the prediction function $\predfn$,
so no choice of $\predfn$ can achieve a smaller risk.
It is the minimum only among [prediction functions](#def-prediction) of the given $\Predvar$:
the [outcome](#def-outcome) may also depend on variables that $\Predvar$ leaves out,
and those variables are part of the unexplained variation $\Outvar - \E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}$.
Measuring one of them and adding it to the variables in $\Predvar$ can lower the residual risk,
as in @exm-irreducible-risk-added-predictor.
[@james2021islr2e, Section 2.1.1, p. 18] makes the same point:
the error term "may contain unmeasured variables that are useful in predicting [$\Outvar$]". <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-irreducible-risk}
#### Residual risk in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor,
$\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar = 0} = 1$ and $\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar = 1} = 1$,
so the residual risk is $\E{\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}} = 1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-irreducible-risk-added-predictor}
#### Adding a predictor lowers the residual risk

Let $\Predvar_1$, $\Predvar_2$ and $\noise$ be [independent](independence.qmd#def-indpt), with $\Var{\Predvar_2} = 1$
and $\Var{\noise} = 1$,
and let $\Outvar = \Predvar_1 + \Predvar_2 + \noise$.
A [prediction](#def-prediction) from $\Predvar_1$ alone has [conditional variance](#def-cond-variance) $\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar_1} = \Var{\Predvar_2} + \Var{\noise} = 2$,
so the residual risk is $2$.
A prediction from $(\Predvar_1, \Predvar_2)$ has conditional variance $\Var{\Outvar \mid \Predvar_1, \Predvar_2} = \Var{\noise} = 1$,
so the residual risk is $1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-reducible-risk}
#### Reducible risk

In the squared-error risk decomposition of @thm-risk-decomposition,
the excess risk from choosing the prediction function $\predfn$ instead of the conditional mean,

$$\E{\sqf{\E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar} - \predfnf{\Predvar}}} \ge 0$$

is the **reducible risk**.

:::

::: {#rem-reducible-risk}
#### When the reducible risk is zero

The reducible risk is zero if and only if $\P(\predfnf{\Predvar} = \E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}) = 1$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-reducible-risk}
#### Reducible risk in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor,
the constant prediction $\predfn_1\paren{\Predvar} = 3$ has reducible risk $5 - 1 = 4$,
and the prediction $\predfn_2\paren{\Predvar} = 4\Predvar$ has reducible risk $2 - 1 = 1$.

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

This characterization of the best predictor under squared error loss follows @hastie2009elements [Section 2.4, eq. 2.11].
The risk identity in @thm-risk-decomposition

$$\E{\sqf{\Outvar - \predfnf{\Predvar}}} = \E{\sqf{\Outvar - \E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar}}} + \E{\sqf{\E{\Outvar \mid \Predvar} - \predfnf{\Predvar}}}$$

shows that the total squared-error risk is the sum of the
residual risk (@def-irreducible-risk)
and the reducible risk (@def-reducible-risk).

:::
